## Verdict: FAIL — three blockers, each a promise a listed test or interface states that no test can fail on

The harness is sound where it is pinned: every gate is green in scope, the four interfaces exist under the design's
names, the four listed tests exist and pass, the negative controls fail as they should and the kernel passes, and the
bars catch real kernel slot dependence (kernel mutants K01 – K05 and K09 are killed by the bars). But three of the
harness's own comparisons can be broken without any test noticing (CONFIRMED by surviving mutants C04, C24, C25, C19):

| # | line | evidence | required change |
|---|---|---|---|
| **B-1** | The listed test "op permutation on every declared-form fixture of M0-a-06 and M0-a-07: identical results" cannot fail through a broken `permutationCompare`: no test shows `permutationCompare` reporting a divergence. | **C04** `permute.ts:166` `compareOutcomes(v.name, ref, runSequenceOutcomes(v))` → `runSequenceOutcomes(seq)` (the variants never run): `C04 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36)`. The only order control (`permute.test.ts` "the control: order is observable…") calls `compareOutcomes` directly on two callback runs, never `permutationCompare`. With the true code the bar does fail on an issue-order kernel: K01 (`tx.ts:159`'s canonical sort removed) is killed by "M0-a-06's batch fixtures (sequences.json): every declared batch, reversed and in 8 random orders". | Add a negative control for `permutationCompare` itself: a declared batch whose applied order follows the issue order must give `identical: false` with the divergence naming the batch — for example a test file that `vi.mock`s `@plat/kernel`'s `tx` to apply a declared batch's ops in the order given (K01's fault) and runs `permutationCompare` on the crowded fixtures. Re-run C04: it must be killed. |
| **B-2** | The bars compare "identical output … bit for bit" (the item's `builds`; C-0199 (1): a commit by its record — created / changed faces by canonical key, in order — the five level digests and the arena print), but no test pins that `outcomePrint` carries the arena or that `recordPrint` carries the dirty faces; the print test checks `arenaPrint` alone. | **C24** `print.ts:336` the commit outcome without `${arenaPrint(p)}`: `C24 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36)`. **C25** `print.ts:311` `faces: r.faces.map(…)` → `faces: [].map(…)`: `C25 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36)`. Either mutant leaves every bar and control green, so a kernel slot dependence visible only in the arena (a flag, a stage rank, a parent of an untouched face) or only in the record's dirty-face lists would pass. (With the true code K05 — the record's created / changed faces in slot order — is killed by the renumbering bar.) | Add tests that `outcomePrint` (and its digest) changes when only the arena changes (e.g. a flag or owner on a face the record does not name, as the print test edits) and when only the record's created / changed lists change (content and order). Re-run C24 and C25: both must be killed. |
| **B-3** | `renumberSlots(plat, seed)` — a listed interface whose contract is "every table rewritten" (item `builds`; C-0199 (2): "the spatial index carried over item by item renamed … its tombstones … renamed") — can leave the tombstone sets unrenamed without any test failing, because the one fixture with tombstones tombstones every slot of its level, so the renaming maps the set onto itself. | **C19** `renumber.ts:352` `tombstones: … new Set([...t].map((k) => rename(l, k)))` → `new Set(t)`: `C19 SURVIVED rc=0 Tests 36 passed (36)`. Probe P1 on that test's arena (`KERNEL_SEQUENCES[0]`, rebuilt after batch 0, then batches 1 – 4): `TOMB L 1 pos 0 2:0 2:1 2:2 2:3 2:4 2:5 2:6 2:7 2:8` (all nine L1 face slots), and after renumbering seeds 21 / 22 `NEWTOMB random 1 2:3 2:5 2:6 2:0 2:1 2:4 2:7 2:2 2:8` — the same set, so `checkIndexState(q)` returns `[]` either way. The mutant is not equivalent: on a partial tombstone set the unrenamed keys filter the wrong items. | Give the index test an arena whose tombstone set is a proper subset of its partition's keys (for example tombstones on vertices or edges after a rebuild taken later in the sequence), and assert that each tombstone key maps through `maps` (or that `checkIndexState` and the queries stay equal). Re-run C19: it must be killed. |

Every other finding is minor and is written to `checks/M0-d-08-notes.md` (N-1 – N-9) for M4.
